items.title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
items.summary: The paper presents a method to perform high‑probability linear regression when noise has only a finite α‑moment (α∈(1,2)) and covariates have limited moments, by reducing to finite‑variance algorithms.
items.whyItMatters: It enables robust regression in heavy‑tailed data, crucial for real‑world AI systems dealing with outliers.

items.title: A Methodologically Rigorous Benchmark of Linear Regression,RNN, and LSTM for S&P 500 Forecasting:Identifying Sources of Performance Inflation in Financial DeepLearning
items.summary: The paper compares linear regression, RNN, and LSTM models for one‑day‑ahead S&P 500 forecasts using a 2006‑2025 dataset with fundamentals, macro, and technical features.
items.whyItMatters: It reveals which deep‑learning methods truly add value over simple models for market prediction.

items.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
items.summary: MemOnce proposes a scalable memory architecture that reduces GPU memory and computational costs for large language models in long-horizon interactions.
items.whyItMatters: It enables more efficient, continuous LLM deployments, appealing to developers seeking lower resource usage.

items.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
items.summary: The paper outlines a comprehensive EEG feature set for classifying ADHD in youth, emphasizing standardized preprocessing, windowing, and quality documentation.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it enables reproducible, high‑accuracy ADHD diagnostics using EEG data.

items.title: Non-penetrating World Models
items.summary: The paper introduces NoPeBench to test and shows that current interactive video world models fail to prevent object penetration, revealing hidden physical knowledge.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers should know these models lack reliable physics, impacting safety and realism in AI-driven simulations.

items.title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
items.summary: The article discusses training transformers that self-optimize their architecture, challenging the fixed-layer convention of traditional models.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because adaptive architectures could boost performance and efficiency in AI systems.

items.title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
items.summary: The paper introduces a ranking‑preserving coreset method to speed up evolutionary hyperparameter optimization by training on a compact dataset that maintains configuration rankings.
items.whyItMatters: It cuts HPO training time, letting tech‑savvy users iterate faster and deploy models more efficiently.

items.title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed
items.summary: The article explains how Hub-and-spoke optimal transport improves long‑context models by replacing dense attention with a linear graph, reducing dilution and speeding inference.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers care because it offers faster, more accurate inference for large‑scale language models.

items.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Agnostic PAC Learning for Partial Concept Classes
items.summary: The paper proves that agnostic PAC learning of partial concept classes with finite VC dimension requires O((d+log(1/δ))/ε²) samples and provides a deterministic learner achieving this bound.
items.whyItMatters: It gives optimal sample complexity for learning incomplete classifiers, crucial for efficient data usage in advanced ML systems.

items.title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
items.summary: BioEmu2 is a generative model that rapidly produces atomically resolved biomolecular dynamics, combining structure prediction, equilibrium sampling, and time evolution.
items.whyItMatters: It enables faster, large-scale simulation of biomolecular motions, accelerating drug discovery and protein engineering.

items.title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement
items.summary: The paper proposes SUAF, a method to learn reward‑independent representations that capture essential statistical dependencies for zero‑shot policy improvement.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers care because it offers a way to transfer knowledge between tasks without extra rewards, speeding up RL.

items.title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning
items.summary: StereoVLM introduces binocular vision-language models that use stereo images to infer accurate metric 3D spatial relationships, overcoming ambiguity in single-view VLMs.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because precise 3D reasoning enables better AR, robotics, and scene understanding.

items.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
items.summary: The paper introduces Star Panoptic Quality, a metric that selectively evaluates split and merged instances in segmentation tasks.
items.whyItMatters: It helps developers assess segmentation quality when annotations are imperfect or ambiguous.

items.title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together
items.summary: The paper shows transformers learn functional depth, meaning layers become interdependent rather than independent refinements, using an inclusion-exclusion decomposition to isolate this effect.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding functional depth helps optimize model depth and training for better performance and efficiency.

items.title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search
items.summary: The article introduces interpretable embeddings using decision columns as an index for explainable entity matching and search.
items.whyItMatters: It offers transparent, auditable matching, enabling tech-savvy users to trust and modify entity resolution without retraining.

items.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs
items.summary: The paper presents a communication‑efficient federated learning framework to learn latent patient representations from multi‑institutional EHR data without sharing raw records.
items.whyItMatters: It enables privacy‑preserving, generalizable health insights across hospitals, boosting AI model robustness and clinical decision support.

items.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search
items.summary: The article presents a Dual‑Tier Sentiment Framework for scalable, automated UX attribution in large‑scale web search, combining macro and micro analysis.
items.whyItMatters: It offers faster, more granular UX insights than surveys, aiding rapid A/B testing and visual‑spatial anomaly detection.

items.title: TEA-Bench-BR: Can Coding Agents Turn a Branching Clinical Specification into Correct Code?
items.summary: The article introduces TEA-Bench-BR, a benchmark for testing coding agents on a Brazilian autism screening pathway, highlighting silent bugs in rule‑based code.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers care because it exposes hidden errors in automated clinical coding, impacting patient safety and data interoperability.

items.title: FairITR: Fairness-Aware Learning of Multicategory Individualized Treatment Rules
items.summary: The paper introduces FairITR, a method for learning multicategory individualized treatment rules that incorporate fairness constraints to avoid biased decisions across sensitive groups.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it balances personalized medicine with equity, reducing algorithmic bias in healthcare decisions.

items.title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think
items.summary: Speculative decoding speeds up language‑model inference by pre‑generating candidate continuations, but its effectiveness hinges on accurately predicting the target model’s future path amid uncertainty.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers care because it can reduce inference latency and resource usage in large‑scale AI deployments.
